html:
The Gabčíkovo Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Danube in southwest Slovakia, part of a joint Czechoslovak and Hungarian scheme agreed in 1977 and put into service by Czechoslovakia alone in 1992.

The plan paired it with a second dam at Nagymaros in Hungary. Protest against the scheme became a rallying point for the Hungarian opposition in the late 1980s, and Hungary pulled out in 1989. Czechoslovakia went ahead and diverted the Danube into a canal on its own side. The two states took the dispute to the International Court of Justice, which ruled in 1997 that both had broken the treaty. The dam still supplies a notable share of Slovakia's electricity.
sum: The Gabčíkovo Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Danube in southwest Slovakia, part of a joint Czechoslovak and Hungarian scheme agreed in 1977 and put into service by Czechoslovakia alone in 1992.
